summary:
The Confirmation Of Congressional Observer Access Act of 2024, or COCOA Act of 2024, amends title III of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (HAVA), 52 U.S.C. 21081 et seq., to codify a State obligation to provide access to designated congressional election observers in elections for Federal office.

Section 2(a) redesignates existing HAVA sections 304 and 305 as sections 305 and 306, respectively, and inserts a new section 304. New HAVA § 304(a) states a congressional finding that Congress has authority, independent of the Act, to send congressional election observers to observe polling locations and other locations where voting results are processed, scanned, tabulated, canvassed, recounted, audited, or certified, or where any other part of the process associated with elections for Federal office occurs, under article I, section 5, clause 1 and article I, section 4, clause 1 of the Constitution. It further provides that the statutory procedures do not establish new authorities or procedures, but furnish a statutory reference for existing congressional authority and activity.

New HAVA § 304(b) requires each State to provide each “designated congressional election observer” for an election for Federal office “full access to clearly observe” all elements of election administration procedures, including areas where ballots are cast, processed, scanned, tabulated, canvassed, recounted, audited, or certified, including pre- and post-election procedures. Observers may not handle ballots or election equipment, advocate for any position or candidate, reduce ballot secrecy or voter privacy, interfere with a voter’s ability to cast a ballot or an election administrator’s duties, or otherwise interfere with election administration. The section preserves the ability of observers to ask questions of election administrators, officials, workers, or other State or local officials.

New HAVA § 304(c) authorizes State or local election officials to remove an observer upon a reasonable basis to believe the observer has engaged in or imminently will engage in federally prohibited intimidation or deceptive practices, or disruption of election administration activities. Within 24 hours after removal, the official must notify the chair and ranking minority member of the House Committee on House Administration or Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, as applicable, and provide written reasons. Mere presence, without additional indicia, is insufficient for removal. A proper removal may be followed by designation of a replacement observer.

New HAVA § 304(d) defines a designated congressional election observer as a House or Senate employee designated in writing by the chair or ranking minority member of the relevant committee, or successor committee, to gather election-related information. New § 304(e) defines “State” to include the States, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Northern Mariana Islands.

Section 2(b) amends HAVA § 401, 52 U.S.C. 21111, to add new § 304 to the provisions enforceable under HAVA’s existing enforcement mechanism. Section 2(c) makes conforming table-of-contents amendments. The Act contains no separate effective date, authorization of appropriations, or appropriation.
